candidate_relations.reason: Laparoscopy placed a solid fleshy mass at the right tubal isthmus, not within the ovary, and histology showed a perivascular spindle-cell tumor rather than a cyst.
The 6.2-cm lesion was fleshy and composed of spindle and epithelioid cells in fibromyxoid stroma, not a mesothelial-lined cystic space.
Rare mitoses, absence of cytologic atypia, and a well-demarcated border contradict leiomyosarcoma.
The mass arose from the fallopian-tube isthmus and showed characteristic perivascular epithelioid cords, not an indeterminate uterine smooth-muscle tumor.
Despite smooth-muscle marker positivity, the loose fibromyxoid stroma and alternating spindle and epithelioid cells around numerous vessels favor angiomyofibroblastoma rather than angioleiomyoma.
A tubal leiomyoma would be formed by intersecting smooth-muscle fascicles, whereas this tumor had perivascular spindle and epithelioid cells in loose fibromyxoid stroma.
At surgery the lesion was a fleshy mass arising from the tubal isthmus, and pathology showed a cellular stromal neoplasm rather than a cyst.

The candidate names the same fallopian-tube angiomyofibroblastoma supported by a benign well-circumscribed perivascular spindle/epithelioid tumor positive for desmin, SMA, estrogen receptor, and progesterone receptor.
Imaging correctly showed a right adnexal tumor, but only surgery and the perivascular fibromyxoid histology identify its tubal angiomyofibroblastoma subtype.
The tumor arose from the right tube and was pan-cytokeratin negative, opposing a uterine adenomatoid tumor of mesothelial differentiation.
Desmin and SMA positivity overlap with leiomyoma, but the numerous vessels with surrounding epithelioid cords and loose fibromyxoid stroma establish a different benign stromal tumor.
